claims.title: Brunei trades with China as Po-ni
claims.summary: Chinese sources record a trading kingdom on the north coast of Borneo, called Po-ni, exchanging tribute and goods with the Chinese empire from around the 6th century.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Brunei: From a maritime empire that once ruled all of Borneo to an oil-rich sultanate, the abode of peace under the world's longest-reigning monarch.", terralore.co/country/BRN/chronicle#ev-518-brunei-trades-with-china-as-po-ni, claim TL:BRN:event:518:brunei-trades-with-china-as-po-ni, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Boni described as a wealthy maritime kingdom
claims.summary: A Chinese account portrays Boni as a prosperous state with a fleet to protect its trade in camphor, spices, and forest products drawn from the Bornean interior.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Brunei: From a maritime empire that once ruled all of Borneo to an oil-rich sultanate, the abode of peace under the world's longest-reigning monarch.", terralore.co/country/BRN/chronicle#ev-1225-boni-described-as-a-wealthy-maritime-kingdom, claim TL:BRN:event:1225:boni-described-as-a-wealthy-maritime-kingdom, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Tributary ties to Majapahit
claims.summary: Brunei comes under the cultural and political influence of the Hindu Javanese empire of Majapahit, to which it pays tribute, while maintaining its long-standing relationship with China.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Brunei: From a maritime empire that once ruled all of Borneo to an oil-rich sultanate, the abode of peace under the world's longest-reigning monarch.", terralore.co/country/BRN/chronicle#ev-1293-tributary-ties-to-majapahit, claim TL:BRN:event:1293:tributary-ties-to-majapahit, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Conversion to Islam and the first sultan
claims.summary: Awang Alak Betatar embraces Islam, takes the title Sultan Muhammad Shah, and becomes the first sultan of Brunei, refounding the state as an Islamic sultanate.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Brunei: From a maritime empire that once ruled all of Borneo to an oil-rich sultanate, the abode of peace under the world's longest-reigning monarch.", terralore.co/country/BRN/chronicle#ev-1363-conversion-to-islam-and-the-first-sultan, claim TL:BRN:event:1363:conversion-to-islam-and-the-first-sultan, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Founding of the ruling dynasty
claims.summary: The line descended from Muhammad Shah, later the House of Bolkiah, establishes itself as Brunei's royal house, beginning a continuous monarchy that endures to the present.

claims.title: Accession of Sultan Bolkiah
claims.summary: Bolkiah, the fifth sultan, comes to the throne and presides over Brunei's golden age, expanding the sultanate's dominion across Borneo and the surrounding seas.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Brunei: From a maritime empire that once ruled all of Borneo to an oil-rich sultanate, the abode of peace under the world's longest-reigning monarch.", terralore.co/country/BRN/chronicle#ev-1485-accession-of-sultan-bolkiah, claim TL:BRN:event:1485:accession-of-sultan-bolkiah, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Empire at its zenith
claims.summary: Under Bolkiah, Brunei's power extends over the whole of Borneo, the Sulu Archipelago, and into the Philippines, with Bruneian influence reaching as far as Manila.

claims.title: Magellan's expedition reaches Brunei
claims.summary: The ships of Ferdinand Magellan's circumnavigation anchor off Brunei and record a wealthy capital ruled by the great Bolkiah, who controls Borneo and neighbouring islands.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Brunei: From a maritime empire that once ruled all of Borneo to an oil-rich sultanate, the abode of peace under the world's longest-reigning monarch.", terralore.co/country/BRN/chronicle#ev-1521-magellan-s-expedition-reaches-brunei, claim TL:BRN:event:1521:magellan-s-expedition-reaches-brunei, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Spanish attack on the capital
claims.summary: A Spanish expedition from the Philippines briefly captures Brunei's capital during a war with the sultanate before being forced to withdraw, signalling the new European challenge.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Brunei: From a maritime empire that once ruled all of Borneo to an oil-rich sultanate, the abode of peace under the world's longest-reigning monarch.", terralore.co/country/BRN/chronicle#ev-1578-spanish-attack-on-the-capital, claim TL:BRN:event:1578:spanish-attack-on-the-capital, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Cession of Sarawak to James Brooke
claims.summary: After helping put down a revolt, the English adventurer James Brooke is made rajah of Sarawak, founding the White Rajah dynasty and beginning the dismemberment of Brunei's territory.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Brunei: From a maritime empire that once ruled all of Borneo to an oil-rich sultanate, the abode of peace under the world's longest-reigning monarch.", terralore.co/country/BRN/chronicle#ev-1841-cession-of-sarawak-to-james-brooke, claim TL:BRN:event:1841:cession-of-sarawak-to-james-brooke, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Labuan ceded to Britain
claims.summary: Brunei cedes the island of Labuan in Brunei Bay to Great Britain, which establishes it as a crown colony, further reducing the sultanate's holdings.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Brunei: From a maritime empire that once ruled all of Borneo to an oil-rich sultanate, the abode of peace under the world's longest-reigning monarch.", terralore.co/country/BRN/chronicle#ev-1846-labuan-ceded-to-britain, claim TL:BRN:event:1846:labuan-ceded-to-britain, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Brunei becomes a British protectorate
claims.summary: Sultan Hashim signs a treaty placing Brunei under British protection, transferring control of its foreign affairs to Britain while preserving the sultanate from absorption.

claims.title: British Residency system imposed
claims.summary: A supplementary agreement installs a British Resident to advise the sultan on all matters but Malay custom and Islam; in practice the Resident comes to run the administration.

claims.title: Oil struck at Seria
claims.summary: The British Malayan Petroleum Company, a Shell enterprise, makes the first commercial oil discovery at Seria, launching the petroleum industry that would make Brunei rich.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Brunei: From a maritime empire that once ruled all of Borneo to an oil-rich sultanate, the abode of peace under the world's longest-reigning monarch.", terralore.co/country/BRN/chronicle#ev-1929-oil-struck-at-seria, claim TL:BRN:event:1929:oil-struck-at-seria, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Japanese occupation begins
claims.summary: Japanese forces land at Kuala Belait and quickly occupy Brunei, seizing the strategically vital Seria oil fields; the occupation lasts until 1945.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Brunei: From a maritime empire that once ruled all of Borneo to an oil-rich sultanate, the abode of peace under the world's longest-reigning monarch.", terralore.co/country/BRN/chronicle#ev-1941-japanese-occupation-begins, claim TL:BRN:event:1941:japanese-occupation-begins, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Allied liberation
claims.summary: Australian troops land in Brunei Bay during the Borneo Campaign, ending the Japanese occupation; the capital and much of the country lie in ruins from the fighting and must be rebuilt after the war.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Brunei: From a maritime empire that once ruled all of Borneo to an oil-rich sultanate, the abode of peace under the world's longest-reigning monarch.", terralore.co/country/BRN/chronicle#ev-1945-allied-liberation, claim TL:BRN:event:1945:allied-liberation, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Constitution grants self-government
claims.summary: A written constitution gives Brunei internal self-government and ends the British Residency, with Britain keeping control of defence and foreign affairs.

claims.title: The Brunei revolt
claims.summary: The Parti Rakyat Brunei's armed wing launches an uprising against the sultanate and the Malaysia plan; British forces crush it within days, and the party is banned.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Brunei: From a maritime empire that once ruled all of Borneo to an oil-rich sultanate, the abode of peace under the world's longest-reigning monarch.", terralore.co/country/BRN/chronicle#ev-1962-the-brunei-revolt, claim TL:BRN:event:1962:the-brunei-revolt, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Brunei stays out of Malaysia
claims.summary: Sultan Omar Ali Saifuddien III decides not to join the new Federation of Malaysia, keeping Brunei on a separate course toward eventual independence.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Brunei: From a maritime empire that once ruled all of Borneo to an oil-rich sultanate, the abode of peace under the world's longest-reigning monarch.", terralore.co/country/BRN/chronicle#ev-1963-brunei-stays-out-of-malaysia, claim TL:BRN:event:1963:brunei-stays-out-of-malaysia, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Accession of Hassanal Bolkiah
claims.summary: Omar Ali Saifuddien III abdicates in favour of his son Hassanal Bolkiah, who becomes the 29th sultan and would go on to be the world's longest-reigning living monarch.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Brunei: From a maritime empire that once ruled all of Borneo to an oil-rich sultanate, the abode of peace under the world's longest-reigning monarch.", terralore.co/country/BRN/chronicle#ev-1967-accession-of-hassanal-bolkiah, claim TL:BRN:event:1967:accession-of-hassanal-bolkiah, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Full independence and Malay Islamic Monarchy
claims.summary: Brunei resumes full sovereignty from Britain; the sultan becomes prime minister and proclaims Melayu Islam Beraja, the Malay Islamic Monarchy, as the national philosophy.

claims.title: Sharia penal code phased in
claims.summary: Brunei begins implementing a strict Sharia penal code in stages, with later phases drawing international condemnation, while pursuing the Wawasan 2035 plan to diversify beyond oil.
